title_lines: Can you hear the difference between a Band 6 essay, and a Band 8 essay?
Today: an essay about volunteer work. Same task. Same topic. Very different scores.
task: Some people think that all students should do unpaid volunteer work in their community as part of their studies.
To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Give reasons for your answer, and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.

blocks: Nowadays, some people think that students should do volunteer work in their community as a part of their studies.
I agree with this opinion because it can give many benefits for students and for society.
Firstly, volunteer work helps students to learn important skills.
When students work in a team to help other people, they learn how to communicate and how to solve problems.
For example, if a student helps in a food bank, he must speak with many different people and organise the food.
These skills are very useful when they find a job in the future.
Students can also make new friends when they do volunteer work together.
Secondly, volunteer work is good for the community.
There are many people who need help, like old people or poor families.
If students spend some time to help them, the community will be more better.
Also, students can feel proud of themselves because they did something good, and I think everyone can enjoy living in a place where people care about each other.
However, some people say that students are already very busy with their homework and exams, so volunteer work can give them too much stress.
I think this is true sometimes, but the school can make a short programme, for example two hours every week, so students have enough time and do not feel tired.
In conclusion, I believe that volunteer work should be a part of the school studies because it teaches students useful skills and helps the community.
The schools should organise it carefully.
flags: “Give benefits” sounds unnatural. Band 8 writes “bring” or “offer”.
Firstly, Secondly and In conclusion are safe but predictable.
“Very” plus a common adjective keeps the range limited.
A double comparative. It should simply be “better”.
I think this is true sometimes,
The opposing view is mentioned, but barely explained.
verdict: The task is answered and the essay is easy to follow.
Few explanations, and only a thin example.
Safe linkers, and errors like “more better”.
verdict_speech: The position is clear, and the ideas are relevant.
But the ideas are stated, not developed.
The linking is mechanical, and there are grammar slips.

blocks: It is often suggested that every student should carry out unpaid community work as part of their education.
I strongly agree with this view, since such experience develops young people’s character while also benefiting the wider community.
To begin with, volunteering exposes students to situations that a classroom can rarely replicate.
A teenager who helps at a local food bank, for instance, learns to cooperate with strangers, manage tasks under pressure and respond with empathy to people from very different backgrounds.
These qualities are highly valued by employers, and they are difficult to acquire through textbooks alone.
Moreover, communities gain tangible support from this arrangement.
Many organisations that assist elderly residents or low-income families are chronically understaffed, so a steady flow of student helpers can make a genuine difference.
Such placements also give students a meaningful sense of purpose beyond their exams.
Over time, students who have contributed in this way are also more likely to remain civically engaged as adults, which strengthens social cohesion.
By contrast, voluntary schemes tend to attract only those who are already motivated, leaving the majority without these opportunities.
Admittedly, critics argue that learners are already overloaded with coursework, and that compulsory volunteering could add to their stress.
While this concern is understandable, it can be addressed through sensible planning.
A modest commitment of two hours per week, scheduled within the school timetable, would leave ample room for study.
In conclusion, the personal and social advantages of community service far outweigh the practical difficulties.
Schools should therefore make it a compulsory, well-organised part of the curriculum.
flags: I strongly agree with this view,
Stated in the introduction and echoed in the conclusion.
A teenager who helps at a local food bank, for instance,
A claim, an explanation and a specific example.
Word partners that native writers actually use.
Concedes the opposing view before answering it.
While this concern is understandable, it can be addressed through sensible planning.
A contrast clause handled with full control.
verdict: Claim, explanation and example in every paragraph.
Precise word choices with only rare slips.
Ideas flow, and the other side is handled with control.
verdict_speech: Same topic. But now every idea is fully developed.
The language is precise and natural.
And the essay flows, with the other side handled with control.

upgrades.label: Position
upgrades.band6: I agree because it can give many benefits.
upgrades.band8: I strongly agree, since it builds character and helps the community.
upgrades.speech: One. Position. Instead of: I agree because it can give many benefits. Write: I strongly agree, since it builds character and helps the community.

upgrades.label: Development
upgrades.band6: He must speak with many different people.
upgrades.band8: Students learn to cooperate with strangers and work under pressure.
upgrades.speech: Two. Development. Don't just state a fact. Explain it, and give an example. Instead of: he must speak with many different people. Write: students learn to cooperate with strangers, and work under pressure.

upgrades.label: Linking
upgrades.speech: Three. Linking. Vary your linkers. Instead of: firstly, and secondly. Try: to begin with, moreover, and admittedly.

upgrades.label: Counterpoint
upgrades.band6: I think this is true sometimes, but…
upgrades.band8: While this concern is understandable, it can be addressed…
upgrades.speech: Four. Counterpoint. Answer the other side with control. Write: while this concern is understandable, it can be addressed through sensible planning.
